evidence_passport.scientific_disclaimer: Terrain evidence quality measures the provenance, spatial resolution, and observation completeness of the underlying elevation data. It is NOT a probability of rover survival, probability of mission success, or calibrated probability of mechanical failure.
evidence_passport.tier_explanation: Assigned 'moderate' tier for official dataset 'Mars MGS MOLA - MEX HRSC Blended DEM Global 200m v2' (Mars_HRSC_MOLA_BlendDEM_Global_200mp_v2) with 100% valid route observation coverage and verified local file integrity because the Jezero Crater sub-window was extracted from the official USGS HTTPS endpoint with verified local SHA-256 integrity, but the full 11.38 GB upstream archive MD5 checksum remains unverified over all source bytes.

source_limitations: Retrieved from official USGS/PDS HTTPS endpoint via GDAL /vsicurl/ HTTP Range extraction; local GeoTIFF SHA-256 integrity is verified.
Full 11.38 GB upstream file MD5 checksum (e98092a06bea74d5ec9a704dcd1fe318) was NOT independently verified over all source bytes because only the Jezero Crater sub-window was streamed.

resolution_assessment.limitation_statement: Actual metric cell resolution at corridor latitude is 189.79 m (X) × 200.0 m (Y) per pixel (effective 200.0 m/px) (nominal equatorial resolution 200.0 m/px; zonal width compressed by cos(lat) at Jezero Crater). Supports regional corridor topographic screening only; does NOT resolve metre-scale boulders, local scarps, sand ripples, or flight-grade rover obstacles.

USGS warns of HRSC/MOLA blending seam inconsistencies and notes the global blended DEM (200 m/px nominal) was originally constructed for global thermal-modelling (THEMIS thermal inertia) rather than precision local surface navigation.
